finding: Al is NOT a data gap — the IAG atlas covers its best lines
prompt: Ryan, 2026-08-09: 'Perhaps some other instruments will help us with Aluminum.'
what_was_claimed: RYA-707's appendix reported Al I 7835/7836 and 8772/8773 as NO DATA, 'outside our wavelength coverage', with ZERO pixels. Register v48 carries that claim.
what_is_true: That was true for HARPS (3783-6910 A) and FALSE for the project. The IAG Reiners+2016 FTS solar flux atlas covers 4047.4-10649.9 A in air and has been loaded as a SECOND ARM by the deblend harnesses since RYA-551. We have had these lines the whole time.
why_it_matters: 8772/8773 is the strongest Al I line available: log gf -0.161 against the -1.569 of 6696 and -1.870 of 6698, and 36.7% deep against 22.8% and 13.5%. Al goes from TWO marginal lines to FOUR, two of them far better than anything used so far — and four lines can actually diagnose the 0.339 dex scatter that two cannot.
the_generator_defect: scripts/plot_unmeasured_lines_rya707.py defines 'our coverage' as data/processed/solar_normalized.csv — ONE instrument. Every NO DATA verdict it has ever emitted is therefore a claim about HARPS, printed as a claim about the Codex. The appendix is meant to prove a blank and it has been proving the wrong thing. This is the same shape as every other defect this week: a label asserted in one place about something living in another. It must take an INSTRUMENT SET, not a file.
corrections_owed: the Al entry in the SPP Appendix A prototype artifact
the stage-2 ledger's OUT_OF_COVERAGE class, same single-instrument assumption
next: re-run the Al ladder on the IAG arm for 7835/7836 and 8772/8773. Both need a NIST gf pull like the one Ryan did for 6696/6698 — the 8772 pull is the higher-value one, since it is the strongest line in the element.
